text:
maya: seeing sustained GPU saturation in eu-west1 for the past 8m, latency up and some 502s. Top offenders are a few enterprise customers and a big batch job.

sre-oncall: thanks, pulling graphs now. is this driven by seq len or request rate?

maya: mostly request rate from two customers, token distribution looks normal. queue depth hitting our per-GPU limits.

jon: confirmed, autoscaler isn't reclaiming because many nodes are pinned to Dedicated pools. we've got limited spare capacity.

lindsey: can we burst-shift non-critical traffic to eu-central1 while we triage? routing policy exists but need to ensure fallbacks for model variants.

sre-oncall: plan: 1) apply temporary per-customer emergency rate caps for the top offenders 2) shift best-effort routes to eu-central 3) open a short quota increase for critical customers if needed.

maya: agree. suggest 60rpm per-customer for the offending ones for 30m then re-evaluate.

jon: I'll prepare the routing change and add a canary to 5% traffic to eu-central.

lindsey: i'm OK with 30m window. tag me if we need dedicated pool redistribution.

sre-oncall: applying per-customer override now:

```
redwoodctl rate-limit set --customer c-91234 --region eu-west1 --limit 60rpm --duration 30m --reason "emergency-eu-west-surge"
redwoodctl rate-limit set --customer c-99881 --region eu-west1 --limit 60rpm --duration 30m --reason "emergency-eu-west-surge"
```

ops-bot: rate-limit applied to c-91234 (60rpm) by @sre-oncall.

ops-bot: rate-limit applied to c-99881 (60rpm) by @sre-oncall.

kevin: rolling a routing policy to shift route /gen/best-effort -> eu-central, start 5% -> 20% if stable.

jon: can we pre-warm model variants in eu-central? otherwise cold-starts will spike latency.

lindsey: already triggered warm-up for the commonly used variants. watching cache hit rates.

marcus: heads up for infra billing — moving traffic and emergency caps may change cost profile. pinging billing.

billing: noted. please add cost tag `incident/1795678901` to any temporary capacity or reserve requests.

maya: so far 30% drop in queue depth after limits. latency trending down. still monitoring for any customer-visible errors.

sre-oncall: leaving the overrides in place for 30m, will extend only if necessary and will contact SEs for impacted customers. create postmortem owner?

jon: i can take postmortem owner. will include root cause, capacity plan, and improvements to soft-failover.

lindsey: follow-up action: add automated detection to propose per-customer throttles when pool saturation > 70% and spare capacity < 2 nodes.

marcus: agree. also document escalation path for Dedicated pools so sales/SEs know thresholds.

maya: thanks all. will keep the channel updated. :thumbsup:
